clue.text: Earth father takes a drink

parts.note: sod is earth, the turf of the ground
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad called Earth orders himself a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link: POP takes A in the sense of having it set beside him, giving SOD + A + POP.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda pop is a fizzy soft drink, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Depression, long lost depression

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so the letter for long is dropped from the word

parts.note: a slump is an economic depression

explanation.surface: A long-lasting depression lifts at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'depression' twice in two senses: the second is the slump, the first a hollow where liquid collects.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or hollow into which liquid drains, a physical depression.

clue.text: Day 1: Blair reverses an early impression on sequential education — prevents a "wet uprising" in the House

definitions.text: prevents a "wet uprising" in the House

parts.note: one can be read as the article a

indicators.note: to reverse is to turn back to front, so the letters for Blair's title run backwards

parts.note: Tony Blair was PM, Prime Minister
a proof is a trial print taken before the final printing
a course is a series of lessons in order

explanation.surface: A day in the life of Tony Blair, with a U-turn on education policy and some damp in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. 'wet uprising in the House' is rising damp in a dwelling, not trouble in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof course is the waterproof layer in a wall that stops rising damp in a house.

clue.text: Not quite drunk (a tricky situation)

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means its last letter is left off

parts.note: pickled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone just shy of drunk finds themselves in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a pickle is an idiom for being in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Rome office earnings outside flipping limit

indicators.note: outside means the word for earnings wraps round the other piece

parts.note: pay is what you earn

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for limit back to front

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit

explanation.surface: An office worker in Rome is furious about a cap on earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild curse on the surface, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The papacy is the office of the Pope, whose seat is in Rome.

clue.text: Hop, black — it'll get you high, straight up

definitions.text: it'll get you high, straight up

parts.note: a hop is a small jump
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: Advice to hop and dress in black for a drug-fuelled high.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump jet is an aircraft that can take off vertically, rising straight up.

clue.text: Judge "Swinging Rope" Day faced by one accused of crime

definitions.text: faced by one accused of crime

indicators.note: swinging suggests the letters are moved about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A hanging judge's nickname, and the defendant who must face him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging' is the anagram signal; the surface pictures a hanging judge's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is peril of conviction, the risk a defendant stands in at trial.

clue.text: Cut down flashing behind missing satellite

indicators.note: behind means the word for cut down comes after the other piece

parts.note: to moon is to flash one's bare backside
less means reduced or cut down in amount

explanation.surface: Someone trims the hedge while a streaker bares their behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing behind' looks like one phrase for mooning, but 'behind' is the placing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonless describes a night with no moon, our satellite, in the sky.

clue.text: Proposal involving more than one party (rough bar about what you're looking for?)

definitions.text: Proposal involving more than one party

parts.note: a joint is slang for a seedy bar or dive
re means about or concerning
the solver is looking for the solution to the clue

explanation.surface: A motion backed by several parties, drafted in a seedy pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint resolution is a formal proposal adopted together by two legislative bodies or parties.

clue.text: Delicate quality of boat on lake

parts.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger vessel
Ness is the Scottish loch, a lake

explanation.surface: A small boat bobbing gently on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link with the boat placed first, as in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentleness or delicacy, a soft quality.

clue.text: Parrot character from opera gets cold

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A soprano's pet parrot catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' is a verb here, to copy, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat or copy someone, which is to imitate them.

clue.text: Advertising for poet

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A poet takes up work in advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is publicity work that markets a product, as advertising does.

clue.text: Literary sibling's after a certain type of computer course

indicators.note: after means the sibling comes behind the computer in the answer

parts.note: Apple makes Mac computers
Charlotte Bronte was one of the literary Bronte sisters; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A Bronte sister pursues a computing course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a course of a meal, not of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple charlotte is a baked fruit pudding served as a dessert course.

clue.text: British river crops devastated by desert force

parts.note: the Camel is a river in Cornwall

indicators.note: devastated crops are wrecked, so their letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A flood on a British river ruins the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is the Camel in Cornwall, not the obvious Cam; 'devastated' turns CROPS into CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camel Corps was a military unit mounted on camels for desert warfare.

clue.text: See 22
Like the adventurous wanderer's essay on travelling without Penny long ago!

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters surround the penny
travelling letters move about, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: d was the symbol for an old penny before decimalisation

explanation.surface: A travel essay written without much thought for Penelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: the shuffled ESSAY ON goes round D. Penelope waited for Odysseus, so 'Penny' tempts.
explanation.definitionFit: Odyssean means relating to Odysseus, the wandering hero, or a long adventurous journey.

clue.text: Live searches you'd be willing to make?

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
quests are searches

explanation.surface: Searches a lively, keen person would be happy to undertake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bequests are gifts left in a will, so they are made by willing.

clue.text: Love to imply, idiotically, one is Zeus?

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: done idiotically is done foolishly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Suggesting, foolishly, that one is the king of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the chief of the gods dwelling on Mount Olympus, one of the Olympians.

clue.text: Reduce the power of measure backing the Spanish complaint

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure

indicators.note: backing means the next words run backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a beef is a grumble or complaint

explanation.surface: A measure supporting a Spanish grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the Spanish article and the grumble together, so the pair reads as a word for weak.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfeeble is to weaken, robbing someone of strength.

clue.text: Film star Derek's studio's top stud

parts.note: Bo Derek was a film star; with the possessive S

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A film star's top stud at the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on Derek's supplies an S here.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield.

clue.text: Put in mind of scorer's first time, entering "1-0"

indicators.note: entering means the next pieces go inside

parts.note: one-nil read as I (Roman one) and NIL

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter

explanation.surface: A goalscorer remembers the moment they made it one-nil.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to implant an idea gradually into someone's mind.

clue.text: Provided raised dicky seat for vehicle

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: if means provided that

indicators.note: dicky means faulty, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fold-out dicky seat in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dicky seat' is a phrase for a rear fold-out seat but 'dicky' is the anagram signal. FIESTA is a Ford car model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fiesta is a model of Ford car, a road vehicle.

clue.text: Game not ended by minor hit with Sue's toasted sandwich

indicators.note: not ended means the last letter is taken off

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters are knocked about

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A croquet game cut short when Sue's lad is struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' rearranges MINOR and SUE into MONSIEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A croque-monsieur is a French toasted ham and cheese sandwich.

clue.text: Catch biblical figure roping one in to get work

indicators.note: roping in means taking something inside
with roping, signals the single letter goes inside

parts.note: to land is to catch a fish
Job is the long-suffering figure of the Old Testament
a means one

explanation.surface: Catch the patient biblical figure and rope him in for work.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a job is an idiom for securing employment.

clue.text: Cheerleader's habit of doubling military unit at border

indicators.note: doubling means the unit is written twice

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a skirt is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An artillery unit patrolling the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A ra-ra skirt is a short flounced skirt worn by cheerleaders.

clue.text: Lord, the destroyer has capsized, trapping a small number

indicators.note: trapping means holding the other piece within
capsized means overturned, so the letters are upset into a new order

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A warship capsizes and traps a few sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' upsets the three letters into SHA; the destroyer is a god, not a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva is the Hindu god known as the destroyer.

clue.text: Mark for restoration an issue of "Cowboy Gear"

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's mark to restore deleted text
a son is an issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Reissuing an edition of a cowboy magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed hat worn by cowboys.

clue.text: Having knowledge of Latin, made money

parts.note: earned means made money

explanation.surface: A Latin scholar who made money from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned can mean having acquired knowledge of something, as in learnt.
